title: CVS - Approach to Diagnosis & the Cardiac Cycle

questions.q: In what exact sequence does Book p48 structure the seven components (1 to 7) of a complete clinical cardiovascular diagnosis?
opts: 1. Etiology -> 2. Structural -> 3. Complications -> 4. Rhythm -> 5. Functional -> 6. Treatment Status -> 7. Precipitating Factor
1. Structural -> 2. Functional -> 3. Etiology -> 4. Rhythm -> 5. Complications -> 6. Precipitating Factor -> 7. Treatment Status
1. Rhythm -> 2. Etiology -> 3. Structural -> 4. Functional -> 5. Treatment Status -> 6. Complications -> 7. Precipitating Factor
1. Functional -> 2. Structural -> 3. Complications -> 4. Etiology -> 5. Precipitating Factor -> 6. Rhythm -> 7. Treatment Status
questions.exp: Book p48 sets out the 7-point Diagnosis format in strict order: (1) Etiology, (2) Structural, (3) Complications, (4) Rhythm, (5) Functional, (6) Treatment Status, and (7) Precipitating Factor. (Book p48)

questions.q: Match parts A to D of the worked clinical diagnosis on Book p48 to their corresponding diagnostic headings — 1) 1. Etiology 2) 2. Structural 3) 3. Complications 4) 4. Rhythm … A) with Atrial Fibrillation B) Rheumatic Heart disease C) Severe Mitral Stenosis with Mild Mitral Regurgitation D) in Congestive Cardiac Failure
questions.exp: In the worked example on Book p48, (1) Etiology = A. Rheumatic Heart disease; (2) Structural = B. Severe Mitral Stenosis with Mild Mitral Regurgitation; (3) Complications = C. in Congestive Cardiac Failure; (4) Rhythm = D. with Atrial Fibrillation. (Book p48)

questions.q: Match parts D to G of the worked clinical diagnosis on Book p48 to their corresponding diagnostic headings — 1) 4. Rhythm 2) 5. Functional 3) 6. Treatment Status 4) 7. Precipitating Factor … A) in NYHA Class III B) not on any treatment C) due to Infective Endocarditis D) with Atrial Fibrillation
questions.exp: In the worked example on Book p48, (4) Rhythm = D. with Atrial Fibrillation; (5) Functional = E. in NYHA Class III; (6) Treatment Status = F. not on any treatment; (7) Precipitating Factor = G. due to Infective Endocarditis. (Book p48)

questions.q: In the model diagnosis on Book p48 — 'Rheumatic Heart disease / ____ / in Congestive Cardiac Failure / with Atrial Fibrillation / in NYHA Class III / not on any treatment / ____' — fill in components B (2. Structural) and G (7. Precipitating Factor).
opts: Severe Mitral Stenosis with Mild Mitral Regurgitation; due to Infective Endocarditis
Moderate Aortic Stenosis with Severe Aortic Regurgitation; due to Non-compliance with diuretics
Isolated Tricuspid Stenosis; due to Acute Pulmonary Embolism
Bicuspid Aortic Valve; due to Thyrotoxicosis
questions.exp: Book p48 gives the verbatim model statement: A. Rheumatic Heart disease, B. Severe Mitral Stenosis with Mild Mitral Regurgitation, C. in Congestive Cardiac Failure, D. with Atrial Fibrillation, E. in NYHA Class III, F. not on any treatment, G. due to Infective Endocarditis. (Book p48)

questions.q: A student presents a case as: 'Rheumatic Heart disease, Severe Mitral Stenosis with Mild Mitral Regurgitation, in NYHA Class III, in Congestive Cardiac Failure, due to Infective Endocarditis, with Atrial Fibrillation, not on any treatment.' According to the 7-point framework on Book p48, which correction restores the mandatory presentation order?
opts: Place Complications ('in Congestive Cardiac Failure') as #3 before Rhythm ('with Atrial Fibrillation', #4), followed by Functional ('in NYHA Class III', #5), Treatment Status ('not on any treatment', #6), and Precipitating Factor ('due to Infective Endocarditis', #7)
Place Precipitating Factor ('due to Infective Endocarditis') immediately after Etiology (#1) and end with Structural (#7)
Omit Treatment Status (#6) and merge Complications (#3) with Functional (#5)
State Rhythm (#1) first, followed by Functional (#2) and Etiology (#3)
questions.exp: Book p48 mandates the 7-part sequence: 1. Etiology (A) -> 2. Structural (B) -> 3. Complications (C: in CCF) -> 4. Rhythm (D: with AF) -> 5. Functional (E: in NYHA Class III) -> 6. Treatment Status (F: not on any treatment) -> 7. Precipitating Factor (G: due to IE). (Book p48)

questions.q: All of the following are explicit headings in the 7-point Diagnosis format on Book p48 EXCEPT:
opts: Functional, Treatment Status, and Precipitating Factor
Echocardiographic Wilkins Score and Coronary Angiographic Syntax Score
questions.exp: The 7 headings on Book p48 are bedside clinical summary categories (Etiology, Structural, Complications, Rhythm, Functional, Treatment Status, Precipitating Factor), not imaging/angiographic scoring systems. (Book p48)

questions.sec: The Cardiac Cycle: Atrial & Ventricular Timing (Circular Diagram)
questions.q: In the circular 'CARDIAC CYCLE' diagram on Book p73, total cycle duration is ____, divided in the inner ring into Atrial Systole of ____ and Atrial Diastole of ____, and in the outer ring into Ventricular Systole of ____ and Ventricular Diastole of ____.
questions.exp: The concentric circular diagram on Book p73 (8 sectors of 0.1 sec each = 0.8 sec total) shows: Atrial systole = 0.1 sec and Atrial diastole = 0.7 sec; Ventricular systole = 0.3 sec and Ventricular diastole = 0.5 sec. (Book p73)

questions.sec: The Cardiac Cycle: Atrial & Ventricular Timing (Circular Diagram)
questions.q: Match each phase of the outer ventricular ring on Book p73 to its sequential position — 1) Three sequential phases of Ventricular Systole [0.3 sec] 2) First two phases of Ventricular Diastole [before AV valve opening] 3) Middle two passive filling phases of Ventricular Diastole 4) Final phase of Ventricular Diastole [coinciding with the 0.1 sec inner-ring Atrial Systole] … A) Protodiastole followed by Isometric [isovolumetric] relaxation B) Isometric [isovolumetric] contraction -> Maximum ejection -> Reduced ejection C) Rapid inflow followed by Diastasis D) Atrial systole [last 0.1 sec of ventricular diastole]
questions.exp: Tracing clockwise around the outer ring of the Book p73 diagram: Ventricular systole (0.3 sec) comprises Isometric contraction -> Maximum ejection -> Reduced ejection; Ventricular diastole (0.5 sec) comprises Protodiastole -> Isometric relaxation -> Rapid inflow -> Diastasis -> Atrial systole (0.1 sec). (Book p73)

questions.sec: The Cardiac Cycle: Atrial & Ventricular Timing (Circular Diagram)
questions.q: Which of the following True/False statements accurately reflects the concentric rings of the Cardiac Cycle diagram on Book p73?
opts: True: Atrial diastole (0.7 sec) spans the entirety of ventricular systole (0.3 sec) plus the first 0.4 sec of ventricular diastole (protodiastole, isometric relaxation, rapid inflow, and diastasis), while atrial systole (0.1 sec) occupies the final 0.1 sec of ventricular diastole
True: Atrial systole (0.1 sec) occurs simultaneously with ventricular isometric contraction at the start of ventricular systole
False: Protodiastole is the very first subphase of ventricular diastole immediately following reduced ejection
False: Diastasis follows rapid inflow and precedes atrial systole in the ventricular diastolic ring
questions.exp: In the Book p73 circular diagram, the 0.1 sec sector of Atrial Systole aligns with the final 0.1 sec of the 0.5 sec Ventricular Diastole (after Diastasis and immediately before Ventricular Isometric Contraction), while the remaining 7 sectors (0.7 sec) constitute Atrial Diastole. (Book p73)

questions.sec: Wiggers Diagram: Pressures, Volumes, Valves, ECG & Heart Sounds
questions.q: Match the lettered phases (a–g) at the top of the Wiggers diagram ('Phases of the Cardiac Cycle') on Book p74 to their physiological labels — 1) Phase a and Phase b 2) Phase c and Phase d 3) Phase e 4) Phase f and Phase g … A) Isovolumetric relaxation [between aortic valve closure and mitral valve opening] B) Phase a = Atrial systole; Phase b = Isovolumetric contraction [between mitral valve closure and aortic valve opening] C) Phase c = Rapid ejection; Phase d = Reduced ejection D) Phase f = Rapid ventricular filling; Phase g = Reduced ventricular filling [diastasis]
questions.exp: The legend at the bottom of the Wiggers diagram on Book p74 identifies: a. Atrial systole; b. Isovolumetric contraction; c. Rapid ejection; d. Reduced ejection; e. Isovolumetric relaxation; f. Rapid filling; g. Reduced filling (diastasis). (Book p74)

questions.sec: Wiggers Diagram: Pressures, Volumes, Valves, ECG & Heart Sounds
questions.q: Match each valve event marked on the Wiggers diagram on Book p74 to the pressure crossover and phase boundary where it occurs — 1) Mitral valve closes 2) Aortic valve opens 3) Aortic valve closes [dicrotic notch / incisura] 4) Mitral valve opens … A) LV pressure rises above aortic diastolic pressure [~80 mmHg] at the end of isovolumetric contraction [b -> c] B) LV pressure rises above LA pressure at the end of atrial systole [a -> b], coinciding with S1 C) LV pressure falls below LA 'v' wave pressure at the end of isovolumetric relaxation [e -> f] D) LV pressure falls below aortic pressure at the end of reduced ejection [d -> e], coinciding with S2
questions.exp: On the pressure traces of Book p74: Mitral valve closes at the LA–LV crossover starting Phase b (S1); Aortic valve opens when LV pressure exceeds aortic pressure (~80 mmHg) starting Phase c; Aortic valve closes when LV pressure drops below aortic pressure (incisura / dicrotic notch) starting Phase e (S2); Mitral valve opens when LV pressure drops below the LA v-wave peak starting Phase f. (Book p74)

questions.sec: Wiggers Diagram: Pressures, Volumes, Valves, ECG & Heart Sounds
questions.q: On the y-axes of the Wiggers diagram on Book p74, left ventricular pressure peaks in systole at ____, aortic pressure oscillates between ____ in systole and ____ in diastole, and left ventricular volume varies between an end-diastolic volume (EDV) of approximately ____ and an end-systolic volume (ESV) of approximately ____.
questions.exp: The vertical scales on the Wiggers diagram on Book p74 plot Pressure (mmHg) with aortic pressure 120/80 mmHg and LV systolic peak 120 mmHg, and Volume (mL) with LV volume plateauing at ~120–130 mL (EDV) during isovolumetric contraction and falling to ~50 mL (ESV) during isovolumetric relaxation. (Book p74)

questions.sec: Wiggers Diagram: Pressures, Volumes, Valves, ECG & Heart Sounds
questions.q: Inspecting the simultaneous Left Atrial pressure, Electrocardiogram, and Phonocardiogram traces on the Wiggers diagram (Book p74), which alignment is correct?
opts: The ECG P wave precedes the atrial 'a' wave and 4th heart sound (Phase a); the QRS complex precedes the 1st heart sound and 'c' wave in isovolumetric contraction (Phase b); the T wave occurs in reduced ejection (Phase d) before aortic closure and the 2nd heart sound; and the LA 'v' wave peaks just as the mitral valve opens, followed by the 3rd heart sound in rapid filling (Phase f)
The QRS complex occurs during rapid filling (Phase f); the P wave coincides with the 2nd heart sound; and the T wave precedes mitral valve closure
The 1st heart sound occurs when the aortic valve opens; the 2nd heart sound occurs when the mitral valve opens; and the 3rd heart sound occurs during isovolumetric relaxation
Left ventricular volume falls most steeply during Phases b and e (isovolumetric contraction and relaxation)
questions.exp: The simultaneous traces on Book p74 show: P wave -> atrial systole ('a' wave, 4th sound, Phase a); QRS -> onset of isovolumetric contraction (mitral closure, 1st sound, 'c' wave, Phase b); T wave -> ventricular repolarisation during reduced ejection (Phase d) prior to aortic valve closure (2nd sound, onset of Phase e); LA 'v' wave builds during systole/isovolumetric relaxation until mitral valve opening, followed by rapid filling (3rd sound, Phase f). (Book p74)

questions.sec: Wiggers Diagram: Pressures, Volumes, Valves, ECG & Heart Sounds
questions.q: When correlating bedside heart sounds and murmurs with the Wiggers diagram on Book p74, during which two lettered phases are BOTH the mitral and aortic valves closed (so left ventricular volume remains completely flat), and what marks the exact transition out of each of those two phases?
opts: Phase b (Isovolumetric contraction, exited when LV pressure exceeds aortic pressure and the aortic valve opens) and Phase e (Isovolumetric relaxation, exited when LV pressure falls below LA pressure and the mitral valve opens)
Phase a (Atrial systole) and Phase g (Diastasis), exited at the P wave and QRS complex respectively
Phase c (Rapid ejection) and Phase f (Rapid filling), exited at the 1st and 2nd heart sounds respectively
Phase d (Reduced ejection) and Phase e (Isovolumetric relaxation), exited at the T wave and dicrotic notch respectively
questions.exp: On Book p74, the LV volume curve is completely flat (horizontal) during Phase b (Isovolumetric contraction: between mitral closure and aortic opening, at EDV ~120–130 mL) and Phase e (Isovolumetric relaxation: between aortic closure and mitral opening, at ESV ~50 mL). (Book p74)

units.title: Approach to Cardiovascular Diagnosis (7-Point Format)
units.guide:
Complete cardiovascular diagnosis order: 1. Etiology -> 2. Structural -> 3. Complications -> 4. Rhythm -> 5. Functional -> 6. Treatment Status -> 7. Precipitating Factor.
Worked model example (A-G): Rheumatic Heart disease (1) / Severe MS with Mild MR (2) / in Congestive Cardiac Failure (3) / with Atrial Fibrillation (4) / in NYHA Class III (5) / not on any treatment (6) / due to Infective Endocarditis (7).

units.title: The Cardiac Cycle: Atrial & Ventricular Timing (0.8 s)
units.sec: The Cardiac Cycle: Atrial & Ventricular Timing (Circular Diagram)
units.guide:
Total cardiac cycle duration is 0.8 sec (8 sectors of 0.1 sec): inner ring = Atrial Systole (0.1 s) + Atrial Diastole (0.7 s); outer ring = Ventricular Systole (0.3 s) + Ventricular Diastole (0.5 s).
Ventricular systole (0.3 s): Isometric contraction -> Maximum ejection -> Reduced ejection; Ventricular diastole (0.5 s): Protodiastole -> Isometric relaxation -> Rapid inflow -> Diastasis -> Atrial systole (final 0.1 s).

units.title: Wiggers Diagram: Pressures, Volumes, Valves, ECG & Sounds
units.sec: Wiggers Diagram: Pressures, Volumes, Valves, ECG & Heart Sounds
units.guide:
Seven phases (a-g): a = Atrial systole, b = Isovolumetric contraction, c = Rapid ejection, d = Reduced ejection, e = Isovolumetric relaxation, f = Rapid filling, g = Reduced filling (diastasis).
Valve crossovers: MV closes at a->b (S1); AV opens at b->c (~80 mmHg, peaking at 120 mmHg); AV closes at d->e (dicrotic notch, S2); MV opens at e->f (v-wave peak, followed by S3 in rapid filling).
LV volume is flat at EDV (~120-130 mL) during Phase b and flat at ESV (~50 mL) during Phase e; P wave precedes Phase a (4th sound), QRS precedes Phase b (1st sound), and T wave occurs in Phase d.
